cf.title: Fix performance of REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY

input.subject: Two issues with REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY

verdict_reasoning: The slowdown in message #1 is reproducible, but the entry has no working design (prior-attempts-1). The author reports in message #20 that v7-0002 never skips a column, and the earlier unconditional skip gives wrong results for the (NULL, NULL) x2 case from message #16. Two level 1b questions also stand: a partial unique index already avoids the slow join (already-exists-1), and the only case is synthetic (demand-1). Confidence is medium because only 3 of 22 messages were read directly.

brief.title: Speed up refresh materialized view concurrently with nullable unique-index columns
brief.problem: Refresh materialized view concurrently becomes much slower when a unique index covers a column full of NULLs, because the diff join compares that column with SQL equality and NULL = NULL never matches. In the reported case the refresh went from about 1700 ms to about 9000 ms after a second unique index on an all-NULL column. Users of concurrent refresh on materialized views with such indexes are affected.
brief.proposed_design: The patch leaves nullable columns out of the full outer join condition in refresh_by_match_merge() and keeps the record equality operator (*=) for the whole row. A later version skips a nullable column only when its index also has a NOT NULL column. In message #20 the author says this guard is never true for materialized views, so the current patch does nothing.
author_claims: The first version cut the reported refresh from about 9000 ms (11000 ms in a later run) to about 3600 ms.
Cases where nullable unique-index columns never hold NULLs may get slightly slower; users can add NOT NULL to recover.
Check and check-world pass with no regressions.
No test is added because the timings are not stable.
In message #20 the author says v7-0002 does not fix the regression, since materialized view columns are never marked NOT NULL.
brief.thread_state: The author found in July that the performance patch is a no-op and proposed going ahead with the duplicate-row fix (CF 6579) alone while looking for another approach. Robert Haas and Yugo Nagata discussed only the correctness fix, and nobody has proposed a new design for the performance issue.
unclear: The material contains no working design for the performance fix after v7-0002 was found to be a no-op.
The author does not say whether a new version is planned for this entry, which is still marked Needs review.
The author does not show how unconditionally skipping nullable columns stays correct for the (NULL, NULL) x2 case ChangAo Chen raised.
No benchmark covers the trade-off where nullable unique-index columns contain no NULLs.
The thread does not say whether the fix targets back branches or only version 20.
search_queries: matview concurrent refresh null unique index
materialized view concurrently full outer join

objections.title: The only two designs tried are either incorrect or a no-op
objections.failure_scenario: A committer reviews entry 6580 as it is listed, Needs review, and commits v7-0002. Concurrent refresh on the reported matview stays about 3 times slower, because the guard never fires. If v7-0002 is relaxed back to the first version to recover the speed, the (NULL, NULL) x2 case is computed wrong again.
objections.argument: Message #20 reports that v7-0002 skips a column only when its index has a NOT NULL column. Matview columns are never marked NOT NULL, so the patch does nothing. The first version skipped nullable columns without a condition, and message #16 shows that version breaks the (NULL, NULL) x2 refresh. Message #20 proposes dropping 0002 and finding another approach, but entry 6580 still asks for review of the dead design.
objections.author_must_show: Which new design removes NULL-key rows from the diff join without matching (NULL, NULL) rows by mistake, and how does it avoid the NOT NULL flag?

critic.reasoning: Message #20 confirms both points: the guarded version never skips a column, and the unguarded version is incorrect for the (NULL, NULL) x2 case. A new design in a later patch version could solve this, so the severity is fixable.

objections.title: A partial unique index already avoids the slow diff join
objections.failure_scenario: A user hits the slowdown from message #1 and waits for a core fix. They could write `create unique index on s(y) where y is not null` today: it enforces the same uniqueness, and refresh_by_match_merge() leaves it out of the join, so the refresh is fast again.
objections.argument: Concurrent refresh uses only unique indexes without a WHERE clause for the join condition, so a partial index takes no part in the diff join. Under the default NULLS DISTINCT, a unique index on y and one on y where y is not null accept the same rows. The thread offers adding NOT NULL as the remedy (message #6), but message #20 says matview columns cannot be NOT NULL, and v7-0002 changes nothing. A committer would likely ask whether a doc note covers the reported case with less risk than changing the join.
objections.author_must_show: Which users cannot replace the full unique index on the nullable column with a partial one, and what does a core change give them?

critic.reasoning: Concurrent refresh ignores unique indexes that have a predicate, and under NULLS DISTINCT a partial index `where y is not null` enforces the same uniqueness. The thread does not discuss this workaround, so the question stands.

objections.title: Only a synthetic case from reading the code, with no field report
objections.failure_scenario: A committer redesigns the diff join in refresh_by_match_merge() for a pattern that may be rare: a matview with a unique index on a mostly-NULL column, refreshed concurrently. Every concurrent refresh then runs the new join logic. If that logic has a correctness bug, all such users get wrong matview contents to speed up a case few of them have.
objections.argument: Message #1 found the slowdown by reading matview.c and showing it with generate_series. Neither it nor any later message reports a production matview hit by it. Message #21 says the delete-and-reinsert path is costly only when there are many such rows. Dropping the extra unique index works around it, since concurrent refresh needs only one usable unique index.
objections.author_must_show: Which real deployments have unique indexes on mostly-NULL matview columns, and why can they not drop that index or refresh without CONCURRENTLY?

critic.reasoning: The only case in the thread is the generate_series example from message #1. Message #21 agrees the path is slow with many such rows, but nobody reports a production matview affected, and the first version showed the correctness risk is real.

refuted.title: The current performance patch is dead code with no working design behind it
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer pushes v7-0002, and no refresh changes, because no materialized view column has attnotnull set. Years later a patch adds NOT NULL support for materialized view columns. That turns on the skip branch, whose correctness for the (NULL, NULL) x2 case has never been run or tested.
refuted.argument: Message #20 shows the guard `index_has_nonnull && !attr->attnotnull` is never true for materialized views, so the patch does nothing. Message #20 also shows that the only fast version, the unconditional skip, gave wrong results for the case in message #16. The entry stays at Needs review with no new design. The author suggests ideas, such as checking for NULLs at refresh time, but none is worked out or measured.
refuted.author_must_show: Which design keeps NULLs distinct in the diff join and also avoids the delete and reinsert of null-key rows, and what does it cost views with no NULLs?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1. The added scenario about future NOT NULL support for materialized view columns rests on a commit of v7-0002, which the author has already asked to set aside in message #20.

refuted.title: Join conditions and duplicate pre-check are coupled with no loud failure
refuted.failure_scenario: v7-0001 builds the pre-check from the same per-column operators that build the full outer join. A later performance patch drops a column from that list. The pre-check silently stops catching duplicates on that column, and the view again misses rows, as in message #1. Users find out only when the view diverges from its base tables.
refuted.argument: Message #17 says the pre-check now uses the per-column equality operators gathered in the same index loop as the join. Message #21 explains that the join gets correct results today only because of NULLs in unique-index columns. So any future change to the join list for issue 2 changes duplicate detection too, and no regression test covers performance. Message #21 also suggests redesigning the whole mechanism, which argues against patching the join list piece by piece.
refuted.author_must_show: How will a future change to the join columns keep the duplicate pre-check correct, and which test would fail if the two drift apart?

critic.reasoning: Dropping a column equality from the shared list makes the pre-check flag more rows as duplicates, as the first version did in message #16. The objection is also about v7-0001, which belongs to entry 6579.

refuted.title: The entry has no working design left to evaluate
refuted.failure_scenario: A reviewer picks CF 6580 from the Needs review list, which has moved through three CommitFests. In message #20 the author says v7-0002 is a no-op and the unguarded version is incorrect. The reviewer spends time on a patch that changes nothing.
refuted.argument: Message #20 shows the index_has_nonnull guard is never true for matviews, so the patch has no effect. It also shows that removing the guard breaks the (NULL, NULL) x2 case from message #16. The only alternatives are one-line ideas, and messages #21 and #22 discuss only the correctness fix.
refuted.author_must_show: What concrete design keeps NULLs in unique-index columns distinct without forcing delete and reinsert, and will it be posted before this CommitFest ends?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1, which states the same point about message #20 with more detail.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The report is on pgsql-bugs, and the thread does not say whether the fix targets back branches or only version 20.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The patch changes the diff join in refresh_by_match_merge(), where a mistake gives wrong matview contents, and adds no test.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Every concurrent refresh runs the changed join, and the author expects a small slowdown when nullable index columns hold no NULLs.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: A partial unique index `where y is not null` already keeps the column out of the diff join.

questions: Which design keeps rows with NULL keys out of the delete-and-reinsert path without matching (NULL, NULL) rows by mistake, given that matview columns are never marked NOT NULL?
Should entry 6580 stay at Needs review, or be withdrawn until a new performance design is posted?
Which users cannot replace the full unique index on the nullable column with a partial index `where y is not null`, and what does a core change give them?
Which real deployments refresh a matview concurrently with a unique index on a mostly-NULL column?
What does the new design cost a concurrent refresh when the nullable unique-index columns hold no NULLs?

committability.owner_note: The owner would need to know the diff logic in refresh_by_match_merge() and record equality semantics. Robert Haas took part in the thread, but only on the duplicate-row fix (CF 6579).
committability.liability: The owner signs for the correctness of concurrent refresh for every matview, with no time limit. A wrong join condition leaves a matview that differs from its query without an error.
committability.author_follow_up: The author stayed through v7, reported in message #20 that v7-0002 does nothing, and said they are looking for another approach. No new version is announced for this entry.

priority.reason: The slowdown needs a unique index on a mostly-NULL matview column, and a partial index avoids it today. The change is confined to matview.c with no user-visible surface, but the current patch does nothing; review cost is a guess because the performance patch was not read.

provisional_note: The v7-0002 patch and messages #4 to #22 were not read directly; the no-op and the (NULL, NULL) x2 failure rest on the brief and the objections' account of messages #16 and #20. A new design would need a fresh review at level 2.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add statistics refresh materialized view
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add per-view statistics for REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW (execution count and last refresh time) to the statistics collector, exposed as new columns in pg_stat_all_tables and its user/sys variants. The aim was to record when and how often each materialized view was refreshed without relying on pg_stat_statements.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Fujii Masao objected that adding columns to pg_stat_all_tables for one utility command is a poor design: it singles out REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW over commands such as TRUNCATE or CLUSTER, would lead to many per-command columns, and the columns would be useless for most entries, which are tables. He also suggested that pg_stat_statements and log_statement could already provide the information per view. The author agreed that these tools may be sufficient for most use cases and withdrew the proposal, and the entry was marked Returned with Feedback.
matched_queries: materialized view concurrently full outer join
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's not good design to add new columns per utility command into
pg_stat_all_tables. Otherwise pg_stat_all_tables will have to have lots of
columns to expose the stats of many utility commands at last.

precedents_retrieved.title: EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW
precedents_retrieved.summary: Allow EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE on REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, showing the plan of the view's defining SELECT (plain EXPLAIN without refreshing, EXPLAIN ANALYZE performing the refresh), analogous to existing EXPLAIN support for CREATE TABLE AS / CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW. A companion patch refactored ExecRefreshMatView into smaller functions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that supporting EXPLAIN would bind REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW to having an explainable SQL plan, constraining future implementations such as incremental view maintenance, while offering little beyond explaining the view's query directly; the author agreed to withdraw the feature. The leftover refactoring patch was also not taken, because John Naylor judged it would conflict with the refactoring in the pending incremental view maintenance patch without helping it.
matched_queries: materialized view concurrently full outer join
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The problem with it is that it
binds us to the assumption that REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW has an
explainable plan.

precedents_retrieved.title: psql: add \si, \sm, \st and \sr functions to show CREATE commands for indexes, matviews, triggers and tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds psql commands \si, \sm, \st and \sr that show the CREATE command for an index, materialized view, trigger or table, in the style of the existing \sf and \sv. Triggers and indexes use pg_get_triggerdef() and pg_indexes.indexdef, while tables and materialized views are rebuilt in psql from extra catalog queries.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the DDL must be fully correct, so psql would need a second copy of pg_dump's DDL logic, which is large and changes often. He said a shared library with pg_dump's knowledge should come first, and noted that the patch fails on older servers and has open search_path security questions. The author did not respond, and the entry was returned with feedback.
matched_queries: matview concurrent refresh null unique index
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This means that, if we accept this feature,
psql will have to know everything pg_dump knows about how to construct the
DDL describing tables, indexes, views, etc.  That is a lot of code, and
it's messy, and it changes nontrivially on a very regular basis.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix for REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW ownership error message
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW so that a permission failure reports "must be owner of materialized view" instead of the generic "must be owner of relation", by passing OBJECT_MATVIEW to the ACL check error path. The author offered to prepare back-patches for released branches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers considered the change cosmetic and argued against back-patching: the existing message is not wrong, and changing behavior in released branches can affect applications that depend on the current text. While writing a regression test, the author found that HEAD/v11 already produced the correct message because of an earlier commit. With no back-patch planned, nothing was left to fix, and the author withdrew the patch.
matched_queries: materialized view concurrently full outer join
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: As the plan is not to backpatch, I’ll withdraw my patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: Incremental Materialized View Maintenance
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add incremental materialized views (CREATE INCREMENTAL MATERIALIZED VIEW) that Postgres keeps current in the same transaction as base table changes, using AFTER triggers and transition tables. The patch computes deltas from the view definition and applies them to the view, with support for joins, some built-in aggregates, EXISTS subqueries and outer joins.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier marked the entry Returned with Feedback after a month with no update. In July 2022 huyajun had reported bugs: a deadlock between TRUNCATE and concurrent INSERT, wrong counts after concurrent DELETEs, crashes on mismatched column lists, and an unwanted unique index on cross joins. The author said he was still working on them. Paquier also noted little design discussion in three years, and Greg Stark had earlier called the patch hard to review.
matched_queries: materialized view concurrently full outer join
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There has been some feedback sent lately and no update
for one month, so I am marking it as RwF for now.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow granting of permission to REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, CLUSTER, and REINDEX
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, CLUSTER and REINDEX grantable to non-owners, instead of being limited to the table owner, by changing the shared permission check RangeVarCallbackOwnsTable(). The preliminary patch reused the TRUNCATE privilege as a proof of concept; the intended design was a single new table privilege (e.g. REFRESH) covering all three operations.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected to spending one of the four free AclMode privilege bits on this, to reusing TRUNCATE, and to the backward-compatibility effect on existing owner ACLs after upgrade. The discussion then turned to how to extend the privilege-bit space (widening AclMode to 64 bits, a varlena aclitem, or a larger fixed-size aclitem) and whether to use one MAINTAIN privilege or finer-grained ones, without reaching agreement. The CommitFest manager noted no activity over two commitfests and that the thread agreed only that the problem of adding privileges extensibly had to be solved first; after no response, the entry was returned with feedback.
matched_queries: materialized view concurrently full outer join
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So I can't see using one of them up for
REFRESH, let alone using three of them up for REFRESH, CLUSTER and
REINDEX.

precedents_retrieved.title: Apply worker fails if a relation is missing on subscriber even if refresh publication has not been refreshed yet
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch would let the logical replication apply worker skip changes for tables that were added to a publication but are not yet in pg_subscription_rel on the subscriber, because ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH PUBLICATION has not been run. It would log a warning instead of failing repeatedly when such a table is missing on the subscriber.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila questioned whether the current ERROR behavior should be changed when no specific use case had been given. He noted that users can avoid the failure loop with the disable_on_error subscription parameter, and that silently skipping changes could surprise users whose subscriber-side setup is incomplete. The author said he had no specific use case, and the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I see your point but not sure if it is worth changing the
current behavior without any specific use case which we want to
address with this change.

precedents_retrieved.title: Range Merge Join
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend the existing Merge Join executor node to also handle range conditions (containment @> / <@ between a range and an element, or scalar BETWEEN-AND / paired inequalities), optionally combined with equality conditions, by adding a range_cond alongside the merge_cond and extending the merge join state machine. The planner would detect such conditions and use estimates to choose this "Range Merge Join" over other strategies.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tomas Vondra's review found that the patch still did not compile with asserts, had no regression tests exercising the new code, and lacked comments explaining the new functions and the reworked executor blocks. Two months later Julien Rouhaud asked whether the author planned to continue; no response from the author is visible before the entry was returned with feedback. Earlier, Jeff Davis had raised concerns about multiple join keys and suggested a CustomScan extension, which the authors declined.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I took a brief look at the patch, and I think there are two main issues
preventing it from moving forward.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found in the corpus. The one objection rests on the earlier attempts inside this thread (messages #6, #16, #20), not on any outside rejection.

The current v7-0002 changes no user-visible behaviour (message #20), and the earlier unconditional skip was withdrawn after the (NULL, NULL) case was raised. A redesign that changes refresh results for existing materialized views, or relies on NOT NULL on matview columns, would need a fresh review from this angle.

The performance patch changes only the diff query that refresh_by_match_merge() builds. It adds no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog entry, protocol message or extension API, and the refresh still writes ordinary inserts and deletes that standbys replay as before. The one catalog change in the thread, the new built-in function in message #14, belongs to the duplicate-row fix and not to this entry.

The proposal changes only the join condition that refresh_by_match_merge() builds for REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY, which already requires ownership of the view. It adds no new privilege, object, setting or exposure, and the duplicate-row error detail shows only rows the owner can already read.
Two objections only. The correctness fix in CF 6579 is outside this entry. Hot-path cost could not be judged because no working performance design exists.
One objection only: the partial-index idiom covers the reported case. Other angles cover the missing working design.
The slowdown is real and reproducible, but the material shows only one synthetic report and no production case.
